objective: Persist already-normalized and already-planned Telnyx contact-attempt reconciliation with recoverable ordering that cannot durably consume a new provider event before its required canonical attempt state transition succeeds.

updatePlan: Execute the canonical attempt compare-and-swap UPDATE first.
Require exactly one changed row before recording the provider-event receipt.
Only after successful CAS record the provider-event receipt with INSERT OR IGNORE.
noOpPlan: Record only the provider-event receipt with INSERT OR IGNORE.

recovery: If CAS fails or changes zero rows, do not persist the provider-event receipt; caller may re-read and re-plan safely.

If CAS succeeds but receipt persistence later fails, provider redelivery is recoverable because the canonical attempt is already advanced; re-planning converts equivalent lifecycle evidence into a no-op and receipt recording can be retried.
Concurrent stale update plans cannot overwrite newer state because CAS predicates include prior state and prior updated_at.
Provider-event receipt insertion remains idempotent through provider plus provider_event_id.
explicitNonClaim: This slice does not claim the CAS update and receipt insertion are one database transaction. It deliberately uses recoverable update-first ordering because a successful D1 batch containing a zero-row CAS would otherwise be able to commit the receipt and swallow retry.
identity: call_control_id must match the canonical attempt providerReference.
Reconciliation cannot change immutable attempt identity.
next: INS-002E2B5 composes provider-reference lookup, re-read/re-plan behavior, and this recoverable executor behind an authenticated-event application boundary without exposing a public webhook route.
